name: FreshBooks
tagline: Invoicing, expenses, time tracking, payments, and accounting for small businesses

pricing.notes: Official pricing URL checked; public 2026 pricing references list Lite around $23/month monthly, with promos and annual discounts.

tiers.name: Select
tiers.limits: Unlimited billable clients; 2 team-member accounts included; custom support and payment terms

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual is an additional 10% lower than standard monthly rates)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Current 90%-off-for-3-months prices are introductory, after which rates return to $23/$43/$70. Extra team members cost $11/user/month; Advanced Payments is $20/month; payroll starts at $40/month plus $6/person.

verdictSummary: For freelancers, invoices, time tracking, and expense logs are buildable; payments, tax/accounting reports, bank feeds, client portal, and reliability make it more than trivial.
coreLoopDIY: Generate invoices, track clients/projects/time, record payments/expenses, export reports, and email PDFs.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because client billing needs to look professional and survive audit/accountant handoff.

priorArt.name: Invoice Ninja
priorArt.desc: Open-source invoicing platform with payments, clients, and quotes.

alternatives.name: ERPNext
alternatives.desc: Accounting, invoices, expenses, time and payment requests in one ERP; simplicity did not survive the migration.

facts.install: Managed Frappe Cloud signup, or the supported Frappe Docker/Bench deployment
facts.dataFormat: Self-hosted companies live in MariaDB site databases with site files and attachments on the server; managed-hosting data lives in the selected Frappe Cloud site.
facts.gapVsPaid: ERPNext covers more accounting functions but is dramatically less simple for a freelancer, with a heavier interface and no equally polished client-facing invoicing, payments, and mobile workflow.
facts.setupBlocker: Self-hosting is an ERP deployment rather than a desktop install: Docker or Bench, MariaDB, Redis, workers, a reverse proxy, backups, upgrades, and country-specific accounting setup.

alternatives.name: Dolibarr
alternatives.desc: Invoices, expenses, time, payments and a real ledger; it looks more back office than front page.

facts.install: DoliWamp, DoliDeb, DoliRPM, Docker, or a conventional PHP web-server installation
facts.dataFormat: Business records live in MySQL, MariaDB, or PostgreSQL, while uploaded and generated documents live in Dolibarr's documents directory or mounted volume.
facts.gapVsPaid: Dolibarr feels like back-office ERP software and its invoice presentation, payment onboarding, client experience, mobile polish, and low-friction time-to-invoice flow lag FreshBooks.
facts.setupBlocker: A packaged desktop-style installer exists on some platforms, but a durable deployment still needs a web server or Docker, database, HTTPS, backups, updates, and localization.

alternatives.name: Manager Desktop
alternatives.desc: A full desktop ledger with invoices, expenses and billable time; collaboration is the part you do not get.

facts.install: Native desktop installer for Windows, macOS, or Linux
facts.dataFormat: Each business is stored in a local .manager file backed by SQLite, including its accounting records and attached documents; the user chooses and backs up that file.
facts.gapVsPaid: Manager Desktop keeps the business in a local file and lacks FreshBooks' easy online collaboration, client portal, managed payment collection, mobile expense capture, and hosted convenience.

alternatives.name: LedgerSMB
alternatives.desc: Serious accounting with invoices, expenses, projects and timecards; the interface assumes you came for the ledger.

facts.install: Docker Compose is the shortest documented path; packages and manual Perl installation also exist
facts.dataFormat: Companies and accounting records live in PostgreSQL databases; uploaded or generated documents live in the configured document store or server volumes.
facts.gapVsPaid: LedgerSMB prioritizes accounting controls over FreshBooks' approachable freelancer workflow, polished invoices, client payments, mobile capture, and low-training interface.
facts.setupBlocker: The first obstacle is a real web stack, Docker, PostgreSQL, administrator credentials, a reverse proxy and TLS for internet use, plus backups and upgrades.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Crater
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Still widely recommended; last push August 2024 and the last release is four years old.

rejectedAlternatives.name: Zoho Invoice
rejectedAlternatives.desc: The free invoicing, time and expense tools are good; full accounting is not part of the product.

notes: Good kinda because freelancers can often DIY most of the core loop.
prompt:
Build me a freelancer invoicing app to replace FreshBooks. Requirements:

- A local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, binds to localhost.
- Tables: clients, projects, time entries, expenses, invoices, payments.
  Invoices get sequential numbers (INV-2026-001).
- Time tracking: a start/stop timer per project plus manual entries;
  uninvoiced time rolls into the next invoice draft at the project's hourly
  rate.
- Invoice PDFs: an HTML template rendered with Puppeteer, my logo and bank
  details from config.json, saved to ./invoices/INV-XXXX.pdf.
- Send an invoice by email via SMTP creds in .env, BCC me; mark paid manually,
  with an overdue list on the home page.
- Expenses: amount, category, optional client, receipt image attached.
- Reports: income by month, unpaid invoices with aging, income by client, and
  a yearly totals CSV export for my accountant.
- No accounts, no telemetry, all data local; nightly copy of the SQLite file
  to ./backups/, keep 30.
- Out of scope: card payments and a client portal, clients get a PDF and pay
  by bank transfer. Skip bank feeds and double-entry accounting.
- README: setup, SMTP config, and how to edit the invoice template.
